### ESLint version

HEAD

### What problem do you want to solve?

On May 5, 2026, Node.js 26 was released.

Ref: https://github.com/nodejs/node/releases/tag/v26.0.0

I've tried adding Node.js 26 to several CI matrices across ESLint repositories, four repositories are currently failing, while the others have no issues.

- https://github.com/eslint/csstree/pull/135
- https://github.com/eslint/eslintrc/pull/231
- https://github.com/eslint/js/pull/747
- https://github.com/eslint/eslint/pull/20847

### What do you think is the correct solution?

Reasons for the failures are as follows:

---

The following three repositories share the same regression that affected Node.js through v25.8.1: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/61971

- https://github.com/eslint/csstree/pull/135
- https://github.com/eslint/eslintrc/pull/231
- https://github.com/eslint/js/pull/747

```txt
file:///home/runner/work/csstree/csstree/node_modules/mocha/node_modules/yargs/yargs:3
const {applyExtends, cjsPlatformShim, Parser, Yargs, processArgv} = require('./build/index.cjs')
```

---

The `eslint` repository is a bit different from the above problem.

The `metascraper` dev-dependencies use `@metascraper/helpers` under the hood, which depends on `re2@1.23.3`. 

However, as of Node.js 26 the V8 engine has been updated, and this package no longer appears compatible. I think we need to wait for it to be updated to support Node.js 26.

`package.json`: https://github.com/microlinkhq/metascraper/blob/master/packages/metascraper-helpers/package.json#L45

CI failure: https://github.com/eslint/eslint/actions/runs/25490068155/job/74795529678

```txt
npm error code 1
npm error path /home/runner/work/eslint/eslint/node_modules/re2
npm error command failed
npm error command sh -c install-from-cache --artifact build/Release/re2.node --host-var RE2_DOWNLOAD_MIRROR --skip-path-var RE2_DOWNLOAD_SKIP_PATH --skip-ver-var RE2_DOWNLOAD_SKIP_VER || node-gyp -j max rebuild
npm error Trying https://github.com/uhop/node-re2/releases/download/1.23.3/linux-x64-147.br ...
npm error Trying https://github.com/uhop/node-re2/releases/download/1.23.3/linux-x64-147.gz ...
npm error Trying https://github.com/uhop/node-re2/releases/download/1.23.3/linux-x64-147 ...
npm error Building locally ...
npm error
npm error > re2@1.23.3 rebuild
npm error > node-gyp -j max rebuild
```

---

I've closed the four failing PRs to reduce clutter, but once Node.js or transitive dependencies are updated, I think it would be good to reopen those PRs and proceed with adding Node.js 26.



### Participation

- [x] I am willing to submit a pull request for this change.

### AI acknowledgment

- [x] I did not use AI to generate this issue report.
- [ ] (If the above is not checked) I have reviewed the AI-generated content before submitting.

### Additional comments

Node.js 26.1 has just been released, but I'm not sure the patches for the `yargs` issue have been applied here. We may need to wait for the next release. (Also, https://github.com/actions/node-versions/blob/main/versions-manifest.json needs to be updated.)

Ref: https://github.com/nodejs/node/releases/tag/v26.1.0

items.body:
### ESLint version

HEAD

### What problem do you want to solve?

Lately we've seen an uptick in AI-generated issues and PRs.

These range from unhelpful, where the person clearly didn't even review what was generated:
https://github.com/eslint/markdown/issues/587
https://github.com/eslint/markdown/pull/590

To helpful:
https://github.com/eslint/csstree/issues/100

The trouble is that it's not always clear if the issue or PR is AI-generated, because if it is, we'll want to treat it more carefully. Also, we'll want to make sure it's not a waste of time because someone opened it without even reading what was generated.



### What do you think is the correct solution?

I think we should add fields to our issue and PR templates that ask people to declare if the issue/PR was generated by AI. Something like:

**AI Acknowledgement**

[ ] I used AI to generate this issue/PR
[ ] I have reviewed AI-generated the content before submitting

### Participation

- [ ] I am willing to submit a pull request for this change.

### Additional comments

I feel like we need to get ahead of this as I'm sure we'll be seeing a lot more in the future.

items.body:
### ESLint version

9.33.0

### What problem do you want to solve?

First, I want to confirm I'm proposing this change for v10, not v9 :)

---

Currently, ESLint uses `chalk@4` to format the stylish output:

https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/d503f1981354c7b86e423879846c61e0405af8fe/package.json#L121

https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/d503f1981354c7b86e423879846c61e0405af8fe/lib/cli-engine/formatters/stylish.js#L7

Node.js added a native ANSI styling utility, `util.styleText`, in v20.12.0:

https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/util.html#utilstyletextformat-text-options

Because `util.styleText` covers the needed functionality, I'd like to propose replacing `chalk` with Node.js' native `styleText` in v10.

Deno supports this API as well, so it should work fine in other environments.

https://docs.deno.com/api/node/util/~/styleText

Upside:
- Reduces dependencies and package size by using a built-in API. (https://pkg-size.dev/chalk@4)
- Makes ESLint more “native” by relying on the runtime instead of a third-party library.

Downside:
- `util.styleText` was introduced in Node.js v20.12.0 but the stable LTS baseline is v22.13.0, so if maximum runtime-stability is a priority, it might be better to wait until support for Node.js 20 is dropped. (However, this API can be used without any flags.)
- If the "stylish" formatter is also used in browser environments, changing it might not be appropriate.

### What do you think is the correct solution?

I would like to suggest replace `chalk` with Node.js' native `styleText` in v10.

### Participation

- [x] I am willing to submit a pull request for this change.

### Additional comments

N/A

items.body:
### What rule do you want to change?

`no-nested-ternary`

### What change do you want to make?

Generate more warnings

### How do you think the change should be implemented?

A new default behavior

### Example code

```js
/* eslint no-nested-ternary: "error" */

// JavaScript code with nested ternary operators

const thing = foo ? bar : baz === qux ? quxx : foobar;
foo ? (baz === qux ? quxx() : foobar()) : bar();

// TypeScript code with nested ternary operators

type KindOf<T> = T extends string
  ? 'string'
  : T extends number
    ? 'number'
    : T extends boolean
      ? 'boolean'
      : T extends any[]
        ? 'array'
        : 'other';
```

### What does the rule currently do for this code?

The `no-nested-ternary` rule currently doesn’t understand TypeScript syntax, so it fails to flag errors when nested  [conditional types](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/2/conditional-types.html) are used.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0e0e846b-a244-4aef-99b8-01cb208885c7)

That’s because the TypeScript AST differs slightly from the JavaScript AST for ternary operations.

[TypeScript AST](https://typescript-eslint.io/play#ts=5.8.3&showAST=es&fileType=.tsx&code=C4TwDgpgBA0glgOwCYHkBmAeAKgPigXiiyggA9gJkBnKK4AJ0QHMBYAKCigH4oByOxgia92nAFxES5SkhoIArgFsARhHqjufBSrUiOUCcTIVqUZQHtzAGwgBDBBp68L1uwj3jJxmTXsgA2gC6jny29PS2IB4GfObAABa6ANzsQA&eslintrc=N4KABGBEBOCuA2BTAzpAXGYBfEWg&tsconfig=N4KABGBEDGD2C2AHAlgGwKYCcDyiAuysAdgM6QBcYoEEkJemy0eAcgK6qoDCAFutAGsylBm3TgwAXxCSgA&tokens=false)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c6b25fc9-5955-493c-ac7b-2f6ea99b4172)

### What will the rule do after it's changed?

For the reasons mentioned above, I’d like to request adding TypeScript syntax support to the `no-nested-ternary` rule.

### Participation

- [x] I am willing to submit a pull request to implement this change.

### Additional comments

This issue is follow-up to https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/19173

items.body:
### ESLint version

v9.22.0

### What problem do you want to solve?

Hello,

Currently, the `Rule.RuleModule` type is not generic, which prevents me from extending the `ExtRuleDocs` property with custom properties.

Please take a look at the source code below.

https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/main/lib/types/index.d.ts#L554-L562

For example:

```js
// @ts-check

/**
 * @typedef {import("eslint").Rule.RuleModule} RuleModule
 */

/** @type {RuleModule} */
export default {
  meta: {
    docs: {
      'my-custom-property': 'my-custom-property' // ❌This line causes a type error❌
      recommended: true,
    },
  },
}
```

When I try to add `my-custom-property` to `meta.docs`, I get a type error because `ExtRuleDocs` is simply initialized as `{}` with no way to extend its functionality.

I’d like to suggest adding support for generic types in `Rule.RuleModule` to allow for greater flexibility.

### What do you think is the correct solution?

- Before: The `RuleModule` type cannot be extended.

```diff
-   type RuleModule = RuleDefinition<{
        LangOptions: Linter.LanguageOptions,
        Code: SourceCode,
        RuleOptions: any[],
        Visitor: NodeListener,
        Node: ESTree.Node,
        MessageIds: string,
-       ExtRuleDocs: {}
    }>;
```

- After: The `RuleModule` type can be extended using generics, allowing users to define custom types.

```diff
+   type RuleModule<ExtRuleDocs = {}> = RuleDefinition<{
        LangOptions: Linter.LanguageOptions,
        Code: SourceCode,
        RuleOptions: any[],
        Visitor: NodeListener,
        Node: ESTree.Node,
        MessageIds: string,
+       ExtRuleDocs: ExtRuleDocs,
    }>;
```

As a result, We can define a custom `ExtRuleDocs` type like the code below:

```js
/**
 * @typedef {import("eslint").Rule.RuleModule<{ 'my-custom-property'?: string }>} RuleModule
 */
```

Please note that this change does not affect ESLint's current behavior. Looking forward to your comments on this!

### Participation

- [x] I am willing to submit a pull request for this change.

### Additional comments

_No response_
